analysis.title: Tech refuses to break now imagine what happens if yields fall
key_insights: Tech has absorbed a sharp rates shock without breaking while the AI capex cycle keeps accelerating. NDX is pressing against a major breakout level as the rates setup improves.
NDX is closing in on 31,200 in futures after months of consolidation. The 50-day moving average has turned higher again. A clean close above 31,200 could produce a squeeze.

Another large selloff hit rates yesterday. USTs sold off hard, OAT/Bund spread widened through 130bp and stress spread to BTPs. The S&P barely moved, and Nasdaq and Russell finished green, so US equities ignored the rates and Europe stress.

GS expects hyperscaler debt issuance to rise to $420bn in 2027, but interest expense remains a very small part of hyperscaler earnings. Higher yields have not derailed capex, so the AI buildout is not rate sensitive.
MS sees combined hyperscaler capex at about $1.4tn in 2027 versus consensus of roughly $1-1.1tn. MS expects another round of upward revisions into Q3 earnings.
MS puts hyperscalers at 0.4x net leverage with cash equal to 132% of debt, so balance sheets are not yet a constraint on the AI buildout.
If long-end yields reverse lower while AI spending continues, a major valuation headwind for tech multiples becomes a tailwind.
Tech held up while bond volatility rose. Previous reversals in bond volatility have coincided with sharp NDX rallies, so a decline in bond vol could add upside pressure.
NDX seasonality is supposed to turn favorable now.

risk_factors: Long-end yields and bond volatility could keep rising, and European rates stress (OAT/Bund, BTPs) could spread to US equities.
NDX could fail at the 31,200 breakout level.
vol_and_positioning: Bond volatility exploded during the recent rates shock while tech held up. Previous reversals in bond vol have coincided with sharp NDX gains.
A clean close above 31,200 in NDX futures could trigger a squeeze.
